    first needs a handshake to negotiate and establish a session. This
    negotiation can be done in user space via one of the several
    existing library implementations, or it can be done in the kernel.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 3b3009ea8abb713b022d94fba95ec270cf6e7eae
Author: Chuck Lever <chuck.lever@oracle.com>
Date:   Mon Apr 17 10:32:26 2023 -0400

    net/handshake: Create a NETLINK service for handling handshake requests
    
    When a kernel consumer needs a transport layer security session, it
    first needs a handshake to negotiate and establish a session. This
    negotiation can be done in user space via one of the several
    existing library implementations, or it can be done in the kernel.
bic_trace_step.reason: In `handshake_req_submit()`, the socket destructor is replaced early: `req->hr_sk->sk_destruct = handshake_sk_destruct;` (line ~144). On early failure paths (e.g., `!hn`, `hn->hn_pending >= hn->hn_pending_max`, `HANDSHAKE_F_NET_DRAINING`, hash add failure, etc.), the code jumps to `out_err` or `out_unlock`, which call `handshake_req_destroy(req)` but do **not** restore the original destructor (`req->hr_odestruct`). This leaves the socket with the overridden destructor, which, when later invoked, will not call the original destructor because `handshake_sk_destruct` returns early if the request is not found (which it won't be, as it was freed and removed). This constitutes the vulnerable construct, and no fix is present in this commit.
